--- title: "GeoPackage (.gpkg) files" format: html: toc: true toc-location: left code-fold: true params: target_dir: "data/Inspect_gpkg" --- ## Overview This notebook inspects **GeoPackage (`.gpkg`)** files. The GeoPackage is an open, standards-based, platform-independent, and self-describing format for transferring geospatial information, originally defined by the Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) in 2014 (). Historically, the **ESRI Shapefile** was the dominant format for vector data. However, the Shapefile has significant preservation risks: it requires at least three separate files (`.shp`, `.shx`, `.dbf`) to function, has a hard 2GB size limit, and truncates column names to 10 characters [@obe2021]. In contrast, the **GeoPackage** is a platform-independent, single-file container based on SQLite. It supports direct use, is self-describing, and eliminates the multi-file fragility of Shapefiles (). **Curation Objectives:** 1. **CRS Validation:** Verify that a **Coordinate Reference System (CRS)** is defined. A missing CRS is a primary cause of non-reproducibility in spatial analysis, as it prevents the data from being correctly aligned with other map layers. 2. **Layer Inventory:** A single GeoPackage can hold multiple datasets (tables). We must inventory all of them to ensure no data is overlooked. 3. **Geometry Profiling:** Determine the geometry type (e.g., `Point`, `Polygon`) and feature count. 4. **Standard Compliance:** Ensure the data conforms to the Simple Features standard (ISO 19125) regarding geometry validity. ## Setup We utilize the **`sf`** package [@sf] for structural analysis, which provides an R implementation of the Simple Features standard [@pebesma2018] and `tmap`[@tmap] for thematic mapping. For visual inspection, we use **`leaflet`** [@leaflet]. ### R Packages If you don't have these packages installed, run this command once in your R console: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # install.packages(c("sf", "tidyverse", "leaflet", "tmap", "tools", "DT")) ``` ::: ### Load libraries This chunk loads the necessary libraries for the session. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) library(sf) library(tmap) library(leaflet) library(tools) library(DT) library(rstudioapi) # Validation check for system dependencies (GDAL/GEOS) if (!require("sf", quietly = TRUE)) { stop("The 'sf' package is missing. Please install it to proceed.") } ``` ::: ## Batch Inventory A GeoPackage is a database that may contain multiple datasets. We rely on sf::st_layers(), which queries the SQLite metadata tables without loading the actual geometry. This allows for rapid scanning of large archives. ### Select Target Directory Select the directory containing the .gpkg files. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Hybrid Selection Logic (Interactive vs Batch) if (interactive() && requireNamespace("rstudioapi", quietly = TRUE)) { message("Running in interactive mode. Please select a directory.") selected_dir <- rstudioapi::selectDirectory(caption = "Select GeoPackage Directory") if (is.null(selected_dir)) stop("No directory selected.") target_dir <- selected_dir } else { target_dir <- params$target_dir } if (!dir.exists(target_dir)) stop(paste("Directory not found:", target_dir)) message("Analyzing directory: ", target_dir) ``` ::: ## Inventory of files ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} gpkg_files <- list.files( path = target_dir, pattern = "\\.gpkg$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE ) message("Found ", length(gpkg_files), " GeoPackage files.") ``` ::: ## Batch Layer Analysis A GeoPackage is technically a relational database (SQLite). Therefore, we cannot simply "read the file"; we must query it to list its Layers (tables). The st_layers() function retrieves metadata without loading the heavy geometry data into memory. **Key Metrics Extracted:** - **Layer Name:** The identifier within the database. - **Geometry:** The topological type (e.g., Polygon, MultiPoint). - **CRS:** The coordinate reference system ID (e.g., EPSG:4326). - **Features:** The number of rows (spatial objects). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} analyze_gpkg_layers <- function(file_path) { fname <- basename(file_path) file_size_mb <- round(file.size(file_path) / 1024^2, 2) tryCatch({ # 1. List Layers (st_layers creates a summary without reading full geometry) layer_info <- st_layers(file_path) # 2. Extract Metadata for each layer # If file has 0 layers, we return a blank record if (length(layer_info$name) == 0) { return(tibble( FileName = fname, Size_MB = file_size_mb, Layer_Name = "EMPTY", Geometry_Type = NA, CRS = NA, Features = 0, Fields = 0, Status = "Empty GPKG" )) } # Map over layers to get details purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(layer_info$name), function(i) { crs_val <- layer_info$crs[[i]] # Extract the CRS input code (e.g. "EPSG:4326") crs_code <- if (!is.na(crs_val)) crs_val$input else "Missing" tibble( FileName = fname, Size_MB = file_size_mb, Layer_Name = layer_info$name[i], Geometry_Type = paste(layer_info$geomtype[[i]], collapse = ", "), CRS = as.character(crs_code), Features = layer_info$features[i], Fields = layer_info$fields[i], Status = "Success" ) }) }, error = function(e) { tibble( FileName = fname, Size_MB = file_size_mb, Layer_Name = NA, Geometry_Type = NA, CRS = NA, Features = NA, Fields = NA, Status = paste("Read Failed:", e$message) ) }) } ``` ::: ### Execute analysis ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} message("Inspecting GeoPackage layers...") layer_report <- purrr::map_dfr(gpkg_files, analyze_gpkg_layers) # Display interactive table datatable(layer_report, options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE), caption = "Table 1: GeoPackage Layer Inventory") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### Visualization Visualizing spatial data is the most effective way to detect Projection Errors. If a layer lacks a CRS or has an incorrect one, points may appear in "Null Island" (0,0 coordinates) or be distorted. We use tmap to plot the first available layer as a diagnostic check. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # 1. Select the first valid layer valid_layers <- layer_report %>% filter(Status == "Success", Features > 0) if (nrow(valid_layers) > 0) { target_file <- file.path(target_dir, valid_layers$FileName[1]) target_layer <- valid_layers$Layer_Name[1] message("Visualizing: ", target_layer, " from ", basename(target_file)) # Read the actual data geo_data <- st_read(target_file, layer = target_layer, quiet = TRUE) # Plot using tmap in static "plot" mode tmap_mode("plot") tm_shape(geo_data) + tm_borders(col = "black", lwd = 1) + tm_fill(col = "#4C78A8", alpha = 0.6) + tm_layout( title = paste0("Layer: ", target_layer), frame = TRUE ) } else { message("No valid spatial layers found to visualize.") } ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Sample Map: First Layer of First File](Inspect_gpkg_Notebook_files/figure-html/viz-map-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ### Save results ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} output_dir <- file.path("Results", "Inspect_GPKG") if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE) output_file <- file.path(output_dir, paste0("GPKG_Layer_Report_", Sys.Date(), ".csv")) write_csv(layer_report, output_file) message("Report saved to: ", output_file) ``` ::: ## Interactive Ground-Truthing (leaflet) While batch scanning validates structure, Visual Inspection validates content. It is the primary method for detecting "logical errors," such as a dataset labeled "Canada" that visually appears in "Australia" due to projection issues [@explorat2024]. We inspect a single file below. This step uses leaflet to overlay the data on a reference base map (OpenStreetMap). **Note:** Leaflet requires the WGS84 coordinate system (EPSG:4326). We perform an on-the-fly transformation to ensure the data renders correctly. ### Select File for Inspection ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Default to the first valid file found, or use the parameter if (exists("layer_report") && nrow(layer_report) > 0) { target_file <- file.path(target_dir, layer_report$FileName[1]) } else { target_file <- params$target_file } message("Inspecting file: ", basename(target_file)) ``` ::: ### Layer Table of Contents (st_layers) Before reading data, we examine the table of contents. This confirms the schema without loading potentially massive datasets into memory. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} st_layers(target_file) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Driver: GPKG Available layers: layer_name geometry_type features fields 1 20230606_cbblackburn3_p1_labels_points Point 43 18 2 20230606_cbblackburn3_p1_labels_masks Polygon 145 3 crs_name 1 WGS 84 / UTM zone 19N 2 WGS 84 / UTM zone 19N ``` ::: ::: ### Statistical Overview (summary) We load a specific layer to check for value distribution. Anomalies in the summary() output (e.g., a "Population" column with negative values) often indicate data corruption. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Read the first layer by default gpkg_data <- st_read(target_file, quiet = TRUE) # Statistical Summary summary(gpkg_data) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` plot class_code scientific_name taxon_id Length:43 Length:43 Length:43 Length:43 Class :character Class :character Class :character Class :character Mode :character Mode :character Mode :character Mode :character planted_natural instrument height1_no_shoot_cm height2_no_shoot_cm Length:43 Length:43 Min. : 0 Min. : 0.0 Class :character Class :character 1st Qu.: 0 1st Qu.: 0.0 Mode :character Mode :character Median : 0 Median : 0.0 Mean :123 Mean :120.5 3rd Qu.:305 3rd Qu.:310.0 Max. :500 Max. :490.0 height3_no_shoot_cm total_height1_cm total_height2_cm total_height3_cm Min. : 0.0 Min. :130 Min. : 0.0 Min. : 0 1st Qu.: 0.0 1st Qu.:315 1st Qu.: 0.0 1st Qu.: 0 Median : 0.0 Median :390 Median : 0.0 Median : 0 Mean :122.6 Mean :397 Mean :141.2 Mean :144 3rd Qu.:295.0 3rd Qu.:490 3rd Qu.:355.0 3rd Qu.:350 Max. :480.0 Max. :600 Max. :520.0 Max. :580 diameter_type diameter1_mm diameter2_mm diameter3_mm Length:43 Min. : 10.00 Min. : 0.00 Min. : 0.0 Class :character 1st Qu.: 48.50 1st Qu.: 0.00 1st Qu.: 0.0 Mode :character Median : 61.00 Median : 0.00 Median : 0.0 Mean : 58.86 Mean :17.88 Mean :17.4 3rd Qu.: 68.00 3rd Qu.:41.50 3rd Qu.:42.0 Max. :114.00 Max. :80.00 Max. :74.0 comments date_mesured geom Length:43 Length:43 POINT :43 Class :character Class :character epsg:32619 : 0 Mode :character Mode :character +proj=utm ...: 0 ``` ::: ::: ## Interactive Ground-Truthing (leaflet) The code below adapts to the geometry type (Point, Line, or Polygon) to prevent rendering errors. It also performs an on-the-fly transformation to WGS84 (EPSG:4326), which is required for web mapping. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # 1. Read the first layer gpkg_data <- st_read(target_file, quiet = TRUE) # 2. Transform to WGS84 for Leaflet gpkg_data_wgs84 <- st_transform(gpkg_data, crs = 4326) # 3. Detect Geometry Type geom_type <- as.character(st_geometry_type(gpkg_data_wgs84)[1]) # 4. Initialize Base Map map <- leaflet(gpkg_data_wgs84) %>% addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) # 5. Conditionally Add Layers if (grepl("POLYGON", geom_type)) { map <- map %>% addPolygons( color = "#4C78A8", weight = 1, fillOpacity = 0.5, popup = ~paste("Feature ID:", seq_len(nrow(gpkg_data_wgs84))) ) } else if (grepl("POINT", geom_type)) { map <- map %>% addCircleMarkers( radius = 5, color = "#4C78A8", stroke = FALSE, fillOpacity = 0.8, popup = ~paste("Feature ID:", seq_len(nrow(gpkg_data_wgs84))) ) } else if (grepl("LINE", geom_type)) { map <- map %>% addPolylines( color = "#4C78A8", weight = 2, opacity = 0.8, popup = ~paste("Feature ID:", seq_len(nrow(gpkg_data_wgs84))) ) } map ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` Figure 1: Interactive verification map. Use zoom to check alignment with the base map. ::: ::: ## 5. Curation Insights Based on the analysis above, curators should look for the following risks: - **Missing CRS:** If the CRS column in Table 1 is "Missing" or NA, the file is technically incomplete. Without a CRS, the data cannot be reliably combined with other datasets. - **Geometry Validity:** The sf package enforces strict topological rules (e.g., polygon lines cannot cross themselves). If st_read throws an error, the geometry is likely invalid and may require repair in QGIS.. - **Empty Layers:** Layers with Features = 0 are often artifacts of a failed export process and should be flagged for removal or documentation. ## Additional tools While R is excellent for detection, other tools are often better suited for repairing geospatial data. Curators should be aware of: - **QGIS (Desktop GIS Software):** is a free, open-source, and extremely powerful Geographic Information System. It's the industry standard for working with geospatial data outside of an programming environment (https://qgis.org). - **DB Browser for SQLite (Database Tool):** Since a `.gpkg` file is fundamentally an SQLite database, you can use a database browser to inspect its raw structure (https://sqlitebrowser.org/). - **GDAL (Command Line):** The `ogr2ogr` command-line utility is the gold standard for batch converting formats (e.g., Shapefile to GeoPackage) and reprojecting data (https://gdal.org) [@warmerdam]. - **Mapshaper:** A web-based tool excellent for simplifying overly complex geometries (e.g., reducing the file size of a detailed coastline) while preserving topology (https://mapshaper.org). ## Using the Non-Interactive R Script For users who want to run this analysis on a server, in a batch job, or from the command line, here is a pure R script that performs the same process. ### The `Inspect_gpkg_Script.R` Script Download the **R Script:** [**`Inspect_gpkg_Script.R`**](Scripts/Inspect_gpkg_Script.R) ### Example HPC Submission Script (`Inspect_gpkg_submit.sh`) ``` bash #!/bin/bash #SBATCH --nodes=1 #SBATCH --ntasks=1 #SBATCH --time=00:20:00 #SBATCH --job-name=gpkg_check # Load R module module load R # IMPORTANT: sf requires GDAL/GEOS. # On many clusters, these are separate modules that must be loaded explicitly. # Check your cluster documentation (e.g., 'module avail gdal') module load gdal module load geos module load proj module load R # Define data directory DATA_DIR="/scratch/your_user/spatial_data" OUTPUT_DIR="/scratch/your_user/spatial_results" # Run Script Rscript Inspect_GPKG_Script.R $DATA_DIR $OUTPUT_DIR ```
